title: Weights of a Weil complex
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$, $k_0=\Fq$,
and let $k=\Fbar$ be the fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$. Fix a prime
$\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$
of $\Ql$, a separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] finite-type
[def-weil-finite-type-morphism] $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$, and
$Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$. Put

$$
 g_Y=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q):
 Y\longrightarrow Y
$$

for the geometric-Frobenius automorphism [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Fix
$\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, $w\in\mathbf R$, and let $K\in
D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,\Qlb)$ be a Weil complex in the category of pairs
[def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Let $a_Y:Y\to\Spec k$ be the structure morphism, with $Ra_Y^!$ its
constructible exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]
at $\Qlb$ (defined for every separated finite-type morphism; no admissibility
hypothesis in the ambient sense of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] is imposed). Use [cor-coef-verdier-weil-equivariance] to take the canonical
dualizing Weil complex $(\omega_Y,\theta_{\omega_Y})$ and require

$$
 \operatorname{For}(\omega_Y)=Ra_Y^!\Qlb,
$$

where $Ra_Y^!$ denotes the exceptional inverse image for the structure
morphism. Require
$\theta_{\omega_Y}:Lg_Y^*\operatorname{For}(\omega_Y)
\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{For}(\omega_Y)$ to be the canonical
functorial Weil lift induced by geometric-Frobenius base change and the
adjunction units and counits, rather than an arbitrary Weil lift. The
internal derived Hom is the operation of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Define
$D_YK$ to be the Weil complex whose underlying complex is

$$
 \operatorname{For}(D_YK)=
 R\mathcal Hom_{\Qlb}\bigl(\operatorname{For}(K),\operatorname{For}(\omega_Y)\bigr),
$$

with the contravariant Weil lift of duality in
[cor-coef-verdier-weil-equivariance], induced by $\theta_K^{-1}$ in the
first Hom variable and $\theta_{\omega_Y}$ in the second. For every
$j\in\mathbf Z$, let $\mathcal H^j(K)$ be the constructible Weil sheaf
whose underlying object is the cohomology object of $\operatorname{For}K$
in the constructible heart [def-weil-constructible-heart]. Here
$\mathcal H^j$ is the common-stage cohomology functor of
[prop-constructible-truncations], extending the cohomology-sheaf notion
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Its Weil datum is the composite
$$
 Lg_Y^*\mathcal H^j(\operatorname{For}K)
 \xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^j(Lg_Y^*\operatorname{For}K)
 \xrightarrow{\mathcal H^j(\theta_K)}\mathcal H^j(\operatorname{For}K),
$$
where the first comparison is that of
[prop-constructible-truncations] for the scheme automorphism $g_Y$.
Apply the mixed-weight predicate of [def-weil-punctual-weights] to
these Weil sheaves. Define

$$
 \Wt_{\iota,\leq w}(K)
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \bigl(\mathcal H^j(K)
 \text{ is \(\iota\)-mixed of weights at most \(w+j\) for every }
 j\in\mathbf Z\bigr),
$$

$$
 \Wt_{\iota,\geq w}(K)\Longleftrightarrow
 \Wt_{\iota,\leq-w}(D_YK).
$$

The complex $K$ is $\iota$-pure of weight $w$ if both predicates hold.

mathlib_searches.query: Weights of a constructible Weil complex: cohomology mixed of weights at most w plus degree, and lower bounds by Verdier duality
mathlib_searches.results: Only canonical cohomological support predicates DerivedCategory.IsGE/IsLE and CochainComplex support notions; these are cohomological degrees, not Frobenius weight bounds.
No hits; Loogle reports unknown identifier 'Weil'. The second Loogle phrasing below is the usable name search.
25 hits, all references to Verdier in general category theory or bibliographic comments; no Weil-complex or mixed-weight declaration.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q56-53a27b210 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the delivery in full: the item (a definition, no new nodes), the base text, the main-20261015 and master blueprint sources (the same text in both), BBD 5.1.8 (p.126) and every newly cited statement. The delivered statement keeps all three predicates (≤w: H^j mixed of weights ≤ w+j; ≥w ⇔ D_YK ≤ −w; pure = both) and every hypothesis. It now cites the existing nodes that type each object, so the meaning is unchanged: (1) the canonical dualizing Weil lift comes from cor-coef-verdier-weil-equivariance, whose ω=Ra^!Λ is the same functor as def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image via def-fix-six-functor-datum item 4; (2) the dual's Weil structure is spelled out as θ_K^{-1} in the first Hom variable and θ_ω in the second, and I checked this is the correct contravariant direction; (3) H^j(K) is made a constructible Weil sheaf through prop-constructible-truncations, which gives common-stage H^i at Q̄_ℓ and Lh^* commuting with H^i for automorphisms h, taken here with h = g_Y, and lands in the heart of def-weil-constructible-heart. That is the input def-weil-punctual-weights requires. Separated and finite type now cite def-weil-proper-morphism and def-weil-finite-type-morphism, which define them. Small cases: K=0 or Y empty satisfy both bounds; on Spec k0 a rank-one sheaf with eigenvalue of weight v gives v≤w and v≥w, so the dual direction is right; K[n] shifts the bound by n, as in BBD. Batch-5 finding: the citation of cor-coef-verdier-weil-equivariance is accepted as outside the assumptions. It is the general Weil equivariance of Verdier duality (sk-thm-sf-package). Neither nt-assume-poincare-duality (isIso_poincareMap for smooth p) nor the trace formula gives it, and it is no step of their proofs. The path ends at lem-pod-derived-automorphism-hom-evaluation, a generic pullback-RHom comparison in unit sk-def-weil. I computed the closure of nt-target-weil-conjectures and nt-target-zeta-rational with the base deps and with the delivered deps: the difference is empty. All four path nodes are already in the closure, reached among others by lem-a1-qbar-curve-duality, lem-a1-local-boundary-duality and sk-l-dl-a1-endpoints. tool_uses (cor-coef-verdier-weil-equivariance, prop-constructible-truncations) accepted as typing tools.
